page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, utilizing simultaneous multithreading with 2 threads per core. The instance is configured with 16 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core CPU performance, with stress-ng single-core tests placing it in the top 25% of evaluated instances. Multi-core CPU performance, however, aligns with the middle 50% average, as demonstrated by a stress-ng multi-core score of 11737.55 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 6523.0. Memory bandwidth is average, measuring 68.67 GB/sec for large block read-only operations and 49.73 GB/sec for large block write operations. A notable performance bottleneck is observed in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, which falls into the bottom 25% tier.

The c2d-highcpu-8 instance offers a cost-efficient profile for compute-bound workloads that do not require high memory density or local NVMe storage. With its dedicated AMD EPYC processor allocation and strong single-core capabilities, it is suited for tasks such as software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight language model inference. However, workloads requiring large datasets in memory or high-speed local disk I/O will face limitations due to the 16 GB RAM ceiling and lack of bundled local storage.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-8 is an x86_64 compute-optimized server featuring 8 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 4 physical cores. This instance provides dedicated CPU allocation but lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators. Performance benchmarks show strong single-core CPU capabilities, ranking in the top 25%, while multi-core performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations fall within the average range. Conversely, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is weak, placing in the bottom 25%. Given its low memory-to-vCPU ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this instance is designed for compute-heavy workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, and lightweight text processing, rather than memory-intensive database applications.
